name: Posada broadside
summary: A cheap sheet that carries a hard black picture and set type. José Guadalupe Posada cut or etched the picture in a metal plate for the press of Antonio Vanegas Arroyo, and the sheet sold in the street.

philosophy.core_thesis: A flat black picture cut in metal, with a hard white line and set type under it, can tell a news story or a joke to a reader who has little money and little time.
design_principles: Print the picture and the text from one forme: a metal relief plate locked next to the type.
Make the figure in solid black with hard white lines; keep the white line at 0.2–0.5 mm.
Make the mid-tone with cross-hatch at 30–60 lines an inch; do not use a screen.
Show a skeleton, a devil or a crowd in an action, with the face turned to the reader.
Put a headline in large type above the picture and a verse or a story in small type below it.
Print on thin paper in pink, green, yellow or white, and let the paper stand for a second colour.
Accept uneven ink, a broken type letter and a slight shift of the plate on the sheet.
anti_patterns: Halftone dots or a photographic tone
Soft grey wash or a smooth gradient
A fine, even engraved line that has no hard black mass
Heavy coated paper with a gloss
A picture that is separate from the text on a clean white page

process.matrix: A plate of type metal or zinc. The engraver cuts it with a burin, or bites it with acid so that the lines stand in relief.
process.press: A platen or a cylinder letterpress that prints the plate and the type in one pull.
process.image_making: The artist draws on the plate, then cuts the white lines with a burin or bites them with acid. The compositor sets the text in type.
process.edition: Thousands of sheets from one plate; the plate wears slowly and the sheets differ only in inking.

inks.strategy: One black letterpress ink. The coloured paper gives the second colour; the printer sometimes adds a red or a blue block.

colours.name: Printed red
colours.role: a second block, used on some sheets

screening.rule: Make a mid-tone with crossed lines at about 45 lines an inch, and make the deep shadow a solid black.

registration.rule: The picture and the type print together, so they stay in register; a second red block can sit 1–2 mm off.

substrate.stock: A thin groundwood paper in pink, green, yellow or white, made for cheap print.
substrate.finish: Uncoated and rough, with visible wood fibre; it browns with age.

surface.impression: A light bite: the plate and the type press a little into the soft paper.
surface.sheen: Matt black ink, flat on the thin sheet.
surface.texture: Solid black masses with a small speckle where the ink did not cover, and crisp white lines.

marks: hard white lines on solid black
picture and type from one forme
show-through of the type on the back

positive: hard white line on solid black

evidence.title: El corrido de la muerte
evidence.maker: José Guadalupe Posada for Antonio Vanegas Arroyo
evidence.credit: Library of Congress via Wikimedia Commons

emotion.target_response: A dry laugh at death and power: the viewer reads a street sheet with a sharp joke and a hard black picture.

use_cases: labels for mezcal and craft beer
book covers for Latin American history
avoid_when: The image needs soft tone, a portrait likeness or a photographic look.
The subject is solemn and the tone must stay quiet.

modifiers.how: Replace the metal plate with a gouged linoleum block, make the black masses larger and add a plain hand-lettered slogan.
Cut the picture in wood, follow the form with parallel lines and print on laid rag paper.
